I'm only familiar with Amsterdam by virtue of having passed through Schiphol airport too many times to count!

If you are looking for actual good pizza in Amsterdam go to La Perla. Buurman&Buurman is also very good. Of course there is a Madame Tussauds which could be good fun. What might be worth a look is Batavia. Easily reached by public transport, it is a copy of a ship that is now in a museum in Fremantle, Australia. It was built using the tools from that time period using methods from that timeperiod. Small by todays standards but last time I was there it was a nice day out. See if you can fit a visit to Pampus in there. It is a fortress island, built to protect the sea that was there, but we had to dredge up the entire province of Flevoland. Which is quite a feat in itself but Pampus now has no goal. I checked and there is a summer dining event thing going on in july. Fun fact: it is where our expression "voor Pampus liggen" comes from. To lie there like Pampus, immovable, useless, not going anywhere, too lazy. They have tour and such but as far as I can see it is mostly meant for schools, if you are planning to go there just make a call after you arrived how and what. Good dining spot, although I do not know the chef they attracted for the summer dining thing. In case the food is bad do not pin it on me.

Throughout NL, you will see vestingsteden, fortified towns, not really grand castles and such. One of these is Naarden, notice the distinct starlike pattern. It has a rather rich history. No july on the agenda yet, but go check if they have a special day when you visit, they will fire the cannons, clothes from ye olden days, the whole thing. A bit off the beaten path, but that is what makes it interesting. Trainstation Naarden-Busssum, short ride from Amsterdam entral, then a short bus ride, say 15 minutes. If no cannons fired, the museum itself is interesting enough.

Besides the already mentioned A'dam spots. Utrecht is rather close, take a train, it is 27 minutes station to station. Avoid Kanaleneiland, not much to see and too many hyped up "immigrants". Nice café's and little bistro's and such right next to the canal, nice shopping, Domtoren(church and tower), Spoorwegmuseum(railroadmuseum), flowermarket, botanical gardens, Rietveld Schöder house, Dick Bruna house, Central Museum, Saint Willibrord church, Nijntje museum, university museum, Zuylen Fortress, Sonnenburgh observatory, Van Schijndel house, Nicolaïchurch, you can rent a boat or kayak, always something nice to do at Tivoli.

Tivoli is one of many "poppodia", they are sort of like what you would call divebars with live music, but most get funding from the city to keep young people occupied so they are mostly aimed at <30, but older and sometimes much older people go there as well, tomorrow there is an open stage for example, 13:00-19:00 at the local poppodium (Vorstin, a former employer) and it is good fun, there have been live performance art (fucking junkies), some exhibits, painting curses, dance classes, battle of the bands, these podiums do all kinds of stuff and it never broke the bank. Another good spot is Winkel van Sinkel, I went to their salsanights with my gf at the time. (Only poppodium where I have been more than once in Amsterdam was Paradiso. Nice venue, okay performances, more about live music than anything else, I went there for the Distillers and a few other bands.) Hoog Catherijne is okay too, lots of shopping, they are also remodeling the place which will last untill 2019, so not sure how good it will be when you get there. You will go through it anyway, the trainstation is right under it. Stairway To Heaven used to be a good rockcafé but sadly they sold all the signed guitars and gold records on the walls and I have not been since, but might be good to check out anyway. Reviews are good, I just checked.

I think Utrecht is more of a "Dutch" Dutch city than Amsterdam, Amsterdam is more international and touristy, even though Utrecht has boatloads of tourists as well. But as soon as you visit both you will see what I mean by this I guess. The problem here is trains do not run all through the night. They do have some trains that do run between certain cities now, but only once per hour. Check if there is a train running when you are here, they alter train times between summer and winter. The Android app NS Reisplanner Xtra can be switched to English(instelingen) so easy to look there for up to date info in case they fuck up something again (old computers with single points of failures makes for fun times though most is switched over now). It also means you have to get one of the imho not so touristfriendly public transportation cards to use the train, but it is bearable. If you do not like the NS app you can use the 9292ov app. It has buses and all in there instead of just trains. Also can be switched to English, top right, instellingen, taal. Might be handy to have anyway. You could also just use Uber to get a taxi to and from Utrecht and that will work at any time of day, but I am not sure of the cost although train will certainly be cheaper. Rotterdam is also not too far off but a bit grimey by my standards and too many area's you really do not want to go to, they had topscores in a list known as Vogelaarwijken (aka worst damn ghetto's we can find in this place) and by 2011 little had changed and still has not last time I checked.

The Betje Boerhavemuseum was of personal interest. It was a little shop that went from generation to generation untill the floor was redone, and they found very old diaries of the wife of the shopkeeper, her name was Betje Boerhaave. I bought the books and it is a nice insight into life in the 1800's. Quite small but nice to see if you are over there already. I do not think they offer the books in English but you could always ask. Nice souvenir if there ever was one.

You can go to the local VVV (every major city has these) or get a personal guide for Utrecht for helpful tips, hits, guides, do not know if they still have maps but likely they do. Another tip: I did on occassion drive to Paris, you can also use the Thalys, to have lunch and/or dinner, and I may or may not stay the night sometimes. A 4-6 to, and 4-6 hours back by car. Train is likely a better option if you intend to get the deposit on the rented car back. French drive like lunatics. Avoid Montmartre and places like it, Moulin Rouge has a nice show, but it is late at night and there have been times ladies in our group were offered cash, and not just to sit and talk. Though that might be a bit much planning and stuff. Ask about the Thalys/trains at the local VVV if you do this. Berlin is also a good option, 6,5 hours by intercity train €39 to get there. Might be more depending upon high season/time you leave. I cannot give any good tips for Berlin. Brussels and Frankfurt are also easily reached by train. But ask the local VVV about this and about what you can do there. I just went and first thing was to book a hotel for 1 night and then see what there was.

I have a family history of back problems, should I take it easy on the deadlifts?
Try to build up muscle in your back, and don't strain yourself too much. If you fuck up your back you're going to be miserable.

Can you be a little more specific about the back problems? I train athletes for a living so I might be able to suggest some exercises with some more information.

Specific diagnoses, where pain is located, during what motions, etc. Be as specific as you can and I should be able to help.
What would you suggest for pain in the lower back and right inbetween the shoulderblades?

Could be a couple of different things or a combination thereof:

1) Not enough water/electrolytes and that's where you're cramping first

2) Poor posture leading to maladaptive muscular use

3) Strength imbalance leading to maladaptive muscular use

4) Flexibility issues leading to maladaptive muscular use

Are you a large breasted woman? That can lead to some of these issues. I'd suggest checking out AthleanX on YouTube for his lat, shoulder (all three heads of the deltoid), upper back, pectoral, and posterior capsule stretches. You can do them in about ten minutes and it'll give you a lot better mobility that will help posture.

Exercise wise I'd suggest adding some chest and back exercises. Things like pushups with your hands directly under your shoulders and keeping your elbows tight to your body will be useful for you. If you can't do them to start, just do negatives. As far as upper back exercises, I'd suggest adding wide grip pull-ups. If you can't do wide grip pull-ups do the same as the push-ups and just start with negatives.

As far as the lower back pain that's usually a lack of glutes and hamstrings strength or tightness in those muscle groups. AthleanX has some great stretch videos for those as well and make sure you address the piriformis muscles with that stretch routine. As far as strength back there, nothing beats deadlifts or Romanian deadlifts as long as you're doing them with good form.

Obviously this is all blind suggestion since I can't actually test your mobility or strength to see what may be lacking. This should set you on the right path, though.
